item.text: {"question_id":"3B.8","answer":"In 2023, formal assembly and association rights coexisted with recurring restrictions, violent dispersal, detention, and incomplete accountability. The constitution recognized peaceful assembly and association, but authorities used advance-notification and authorization requirements to restrict opposition and civil-society protests; government generally respected association, although registration was burdensome and some groups reported obstruction (BATCH-0011-E011). Police used tear gas, beatings, arrests, and movement blocks against opposition activity in May, including a peaceful Kinshasa march in which at least 30 people were seriously injured, a child was beaten, and approximately 20 demonstrators were arbitrarily detained; three officers were detained, but their military-court trial remained pending (BATCH-0002-E011; BATCH-0002-E012; BATCH-0003-E003; BATCH-0003-E004; BATCH-0011-E011). In January, police used tear gas against an unauthorized Goma protest and detained participants and journalists; in December, authorities prohibited an opposition march and deployed police, vehicles, and armored vehicles to prevent gatherings (BATCH-0008-E008; BATCH-0021-E009). The August 30 Goma operation was substantially more severe: authorities banned the protest, security forces killed at least 56 people according to the official count, injured more than 80, and arrested more than 150; Amnesty’s investigation characterized it as a planned operation against an unarmed group, while four of six tried officers were convicted, investigations were incomplete, and victim remedies remained inadequate (BATCH-0011-E018). Dissent and political organization also faced pressure through journalist detention and prosecution, including Stanis Bujakera, and reported instructions restricting opposition campaign coverage (BATCH-0025-E012; BATCH-0002-E015). Qualifying evidence shows that police escorted a peaceful October Goma march and that a government minister arranged medical transport for an attacked journalist, but accountability for attacks by ruling-party supporters was unresolved (BATCH-0022-E014; BATCH-0027-E002). Tshisekedi’s direct attribution is clearest in his public congratulation of the police chief after the May crackdown; the supplied evidence does not establish that he personally ordered each local restriction or the Goma killings. The severity is therefore widespread and recurring, with one exceptionally grave state-force episode, rather than established nationwide systematic terror.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0003-E004","BATCH-0008-E008","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0002-E015"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0027-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not establish how consistently peaceful protests were protected outside reported incidents.","The Goma death toll is disputed, and the complete accountability, forensic, and remedy record remains unresolved.","The evidence does not establish a direct presidential order for each local restriction or for the Goma killings, although it documents national-government responsibility, senior provincial command, and Tshisekedi’s public praise after the May operation.","The legality of particular bans and the merits of individual prosecutions remain partly unresolved.","The campaign-period chain of command for restrictions on journalists and opposition coverage is not independently established.","BATCH-0009-E001 was excluded as not directly probative of protection for protest, dissent, or organization; it concerns electoral materials, voters, and electoral violence."],"corrections_made":["Removed BATCH-0009-E001 as irrelevant to this question’s protest, dissent, and organization nexus.","Added the January Goma repression, December 27 banned march and armored deployment, and campaign-period journalist/opposition restrictions identified by the critic.","Preserved contrary evidence on escorted peaceful protest and government assistance to an attacked journalist.","Recalibrated the characterization to widespread and recurring restrictions with one exceptionally grave episode, while retaining uncertainty about presidential command and remedies."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A complete ledger review could clarify whether additional 2023 protests were protected or restricted and whether the reported incidents formed a nationally coordinated pattern.","Further judicial and forensic records could materially change the assessment of accountability and remedy for the May and August operations.","Evidence establishing or disproving presidential knowledge, command, encouragement, tolerance, or obstruction of remedy could change attribution."]}
